headline: SPARC gain demonstration pending
interpretation: Tokamak heritage and magnet achievement support a testable path, but the planned high-field burning plasma remains to be demonstrated.

headline: Shared D-T engineering burden
interpretation: An ARC plant must combine tritium breeding, neutron shielding, heat exhaust and maintainable components. A successful SPARC result would not by itself validate those plant systems.

headline: Energy-boundary proof remains essential
interpretation: A recoverable capacitor-bank signal must be distinguished from recycled input electricity; sustained whole-plant net output is a separate milestone.

headline: Advanced-fuel transition
interpretation: Current D-T results do not demonstrate commercial D-He3 conditions, helium-3 supply or a closed fuel cycle. Reduced neutron production is not zero-neutron operation.

headline: Aggressive company schedule
interpretation: The 2028 construction programme depends on physics, repetition, components and electricity balance progressing together. Construction alone does not validate these.

headline: Advanced-fuel energy balance unproven
interpretation: FRC formation is a distinct achievement from p-B11 fusion gain; beam power and radiation losses must be balanced at much more demanding operating conditions.

headline: Roadmap and fuel options evolving
interpretation: Skipping Copernicus concentrates validation in later development. Prospective lunar helium-3 supply is an option, not available operating fuel.

headline: Proposed merger and debt differ from equity
interpretation: The filed merger is not verified closed; the supplied convertible note and additional available facility must remain separate from historic equity totals.

headline: Compact central-column constraints
interpretation: A low-aspect-ratio D-T reactor must fit shielding, magnets and breeding structures into restricted space while handling heat and neutron exposure.

headline: Component success is not burning-plasma success
interpretation: Demo4 verifies magnet behavior; a complete HTS fusion plant still requires integrated plasma, fuel-cycle and power systems.

headline: Three-dimensional reactor integration
interpretation: Coil construction, neutron shielding, blanket access and maintenance must work together in the complete stellarator geometry.

headline: Heritage is not the company’s demonstration
interpretation: Results from HSX and W7-X inform the design; they do not count as achieved Infinity One or Infinity Two milestones.

headline: D-T supply and breeding required
interpretation: Electricity deployment also requires a workable tritium cycle and durable neutron-exposed systems.

headline: Burning-plasma extrapolation pending
interpretation: W7-X supports the confinement approach; a compact high-field D-T plant requires additional physics and engineering validation.

headline: Integrated high-field stellarator burden
interpretation: Complex HTS coils, heat exhaust, tritium breeding and maintainability must be demonstrated together.

headline: Mixed and committed funding
interpretation: The reported cumulative total includes grants, and Bavaria’s commitment differs from received financing.

headline: Complexity shifts into many controlled coils
interpretation: Simple coil shapes can ease manufacturing, while the integrated machine must validate many currents, connections and field-control interactions.

headline: Component and design stages
interpretation: Canis is a subsystem demonstration; Helios capacity factor, net power and coil lifetime are calculations, not operating records.

headline: Later D-T conversion
interpretation: Eos D-D operation would not alone demonstrate Helios tritium breeding and reactor materials performance.

headline: Novel integrated fabrication
interpretation: Reactor-scale patterned HTS manufacturing and liquid-metal flow in strong magnetic fields need integrated validation.

headline: Component stage
interpretation: The reviewed evidence does not establish operating reactor-level confinement or energy balance.

headline: End-loss control remains central
interpretation: Mirror geometry is mechanically attractive but must retain enough particles and energy at useful fusion conditions.

headline: Recovery is not generation proof
interpretation: The demonstrated converter largely recycled input heating. D-T net power requires fusion gain, neutron-heat conversion and complete plant accounting.

headline: Different quantities need separate axes
interpretation: Long pulses, small-magnet peak field and equivalent Q should not be treated as equivalent to burning-plasma or whole-plant performance.

headline: Some financial and fuel details unresolved
interpretation: The current campaign fuel and composition of survey funding are not established here; these are evidence gaps rather than proof of technical failure.

headline: Representative conditions required
interpretation: Thermal-loop testing must eventually connect to reactor neutron environments and reliable tritium recovery.

headline: Customer and industry timing
interpretation: Supplier revenues depend partly on customers’ plant schedules; core plasma-gain risk belongs to those reactor projects.

headline: Early experimental stage
interpretation: The cited temperature and pulsed-power hardware do not establish fusion gain, confinement at reactor conditions or net output.

headline: Power density and shielding challenge
interpretation: A small D-T plant must integrate heating, neutron shielding, heat capture and tritium systems within its intended compact package.

headline: Complex coil and blanket integration
interpretation: Cable and manufacturing advances do not yet establish integrated plasma, liquid-metal blanket and power-cycle performance.

headline: Mixed total with source discrepancy
interpretation: Cumulative financing includes grants and loans, and Japanese/English totals differ. The newer Japanese total is preferred with an explicit annotation.

headline: Physics scaling
interpretation: High gain is simulated for larger, manufacturable targets; NIF validates a predecessor regime but does not validate this full design.

headline: Repetition and manufacturing
interpretation: Efficient 10 MJ shots at 10 Hz, economical cryogenic targets, injection and chamber recovery must work together continuously.

headline: Fuel and materials
interpretation: A DT power plant still needs tritium breeding, heat extraction, radiation-tolerant optics and maintainable first-wall systems.

headline: Physics scaling
interpretation: Driver progress must translate to repeatable high-yield target implosions; peak driver power is not fusion output.

headline: Integrated plant
interpretation: Stored-energy facility gain excludes conversion losses and other plant electricity. Repetition, debris, target replacement and balance of plant remain.

headline: Financing
interpretation: Headline commitments are not identical to cash received; the company reports a newer cumulative amount without a tranche reconciliation.

headline: Driver scaling
interpretation: Excimer/SBS proof of concept must scale to multi-megajoule energy, efficiency and sustained repetition.

headline: Liquid wall and fuel
interpretation: Renewing molten salt may protect the wall, but whole-plant breeding, corrosion, flow recovery and remote maintenance still require validation.

headline: Evidence boundary
interpretation: DOE design-milestone acceptance is not a plant operating licence or proof of commercial energy production.

headline: Target physics
interpretation: Direct drive/fast ignition must establish its own reliable gain regime; NIF indirect-drive ignition does not directly validate it.

headline: Manufacturing and repetition
interpretation: High-rate lasers, target manufacture, precision injection and chamber recovery must be integrated.

headline: Fuel and plant
interpretation: DT breeding, materials durability and heat conversion remain whole-plant requirements despite siting/industrial partnerships.

headline: Physics scaling
interpretation: Higher electron temperature does not establish adequate ion temperature, confinement and density simultaneously. LM26 still targets additional large steps.

headline: Prototype to plant
interpretation: Solid-liner experiment to repetitive liquid-metal machinery is a substantial engineering transition.

headline: Capital and execution
interpretation: Public-market access changes financing options; approximately $150 million cash is not full power-plant financing.

headline: Plasma stability
interpretation: Sheared-flow stabilization must hold at higher current and useful fusion gain; pressure alone cannot rank overall reactor performance.

headline: Repetition and electrodes
interpretation: Repetitive power, electrode erosion and liquid-metal handling need validation at fusion heat and neutron loads.

headline: Business scope
interpretation: Any future fission electricity must not be counted as demonstrated fusion electricity.

headline: Integrated physics
interpretation: Compression and rapid ignition must work together; a successful first stage does not validate high gain.

headline: Partner dependence
interpretation: Target-system developer depends on partners for drivers, facilities and industrial integration.

headline: Commercial systems
interpretation: High modeled gain does not resolve target production, tritium breeding, chamber endurance or cost.

headline: Physics
interpretation: Company-specific hollow-shell fast ignition must demonstrate gain; NIF indirect-drive success is not direct validation.

headline: Laser scaling
interpretation: High-efficiency, high-repetition short-pulse lasers must scale from demonstrations to plant energy and reliability.

headline: Fuel
interpretation: Current near-term design uses DT and retains breeding/neutron challenges; older proton-boron descriptions should not be copied forward.

headline: Physics
interpretation: Voltage, confinement and compact size are enabling results; energy-positive distributions and fusion output remain unproven in reviewed evidence.

headline: Fuel and scale
interpretation: A practical DT microreactor still needs shielding, fuel supply, heat removal and conversion, which affect complete-system size.

headline: Licensing
interpretation: A planned licensed test service is distinct from an operating electricity plant.

headline: Integration
interpretation: Target tracking and repetitive irradiation must be coupled to adequate driver energy and gain on real fuel.

headline: Laser and plant
interpretation: High-power laser efficiency, thermal management and integrated DT fuel cycle remain outstanding.

headline: Funding comparability
interpretation: JPY 6 billion includes debt; do not label it equity or convert with an undocumented exchange rate.

headline: Physics
interpretation: Demonstrated reaction yield is far from a demonstrated self-sustaining high-gain regime; cited paper notes lack of evidence for yield-amplifying cascades in most prior experiments.

headline: Driver and conversion
interpretation: High-efficiency repetitive lasers and integrated useful-energy recovery remain necessary even if the primary fuel cycle avoids tritium breeding.

headline: Evidence and funding
interpretation: Current cumulative company funding was not established in reviewed primary sources. Project value is not a substitute.

headline: Physics
interpretation: Dense-plasma-focus neutron-source performance does not demonstrate the proposed MagLIF plant gain.

headline: Repetition and plant
interpretation: Practical repetition, debris clearing, target replacement and electric conversion need system validation.

headline: Business metrics
interpretation: Radiation-testing contracts, contract-vehicle ceilings and revenue must not be charted as fusion electricity or equity funding.

headline: Substantial extrapolation from experimental operation to repetitive reactor performance.
interpretation: Substantial extrapolation from experimental operation to repetitive reactor performance.

headline: A magnet test and an equivalent-Q target leave fuel cycle, heat exhaust, maintenance and integrated electricity unproven.
interpretation: A magnet test and an equivalent-Q target leave fuel cycle, heat exhaust, maintenance and integrated electricity unproven.

headline: Reactor-relevant confinement, temperature and gain must be shown beyond prototype operation.
interpretation: Reactor-relevant confinement, temperature and gain must be shown beyond prototype operation.

headline: A superconducting magnet within the chamber creates distinctive shielding, cooling, access and lifetime requirements.
interpretation: A superconducting magnet within the chamber creates distinctive shielding, cooling, access and lifetime requirements.
